goal: Hydrate T-KRP-E with repo-local research and exploration evidence before governed delivery.
limitations: Network access was unavailable in the Codex sandbox, so this capsule uses repo-local evidence only.
This capsule authorizes planning hydration only; implementation requires a later governed T-KRP-E scope.
Wave A and Wave B were read-only; no runtime behavior was validated in this capsule.

questions.question: Can existing repo-local Karpathy follow-on evidence be reused for T-KRP-E planning?
questions.answer: Yes. T-KRP-A through T-KRP-D capsules and specs establish the initiative boundaries and repeatedly reserve structured-autonomy success-criteria gating for T-KRP-E.

questions.question: Is the current AD-HOC planning repair sufficiently researched before hydration?
questions.answer: Yes. Wave A identified the task-level boundary and Wave B confirmed the exact hydration write set: backlog row plus T-KRP-E spec.

questions.question: What should the future T-KRP-E governed delivery own?
questions.answer: The future delivery should add a goal-to-success-criteria gate to structured-autonomy-plan so plans derive falsifiable success criteria before task decomposition and map those criteria to validation and tests.

local_sources.use: Confirms T-KRP-E is the active INI-KRP-001 slice in v0.2.0-p3 and is planned as governed M1 work.
Distinguishes T-KRP-D orchestrator assumption surfacing from T-KRP-E structured success-criteria gating.
Explicitly reserves structured-autonomy success-criteria gating for T-KRP-E.
Shows the current planning contract and extension point for falsifiable success criteria.
Provides the repo-native hydrate-task path for turning a planned roadmap task into backlog/spec state.

implications_for_azoth: T-KRP-E should make success criteria explicit before planner-to-builder handoff.
The future gate should map each success criterion to task validation and test strategy.
T-KRP-E strengthens T-006 revise-and-continue loops by making the target of replay falsifiable and stable.
The slice should stay inside structured-autonomy-plan and must not mutate root CLAUDE.md, karpathy-principles, Builder posture, Orchestrator classification, or D23 routing.
risks: The future implementation could accidentally become a new pipeline stage or governance rule; keep it a structured-autonomy-plan quality gate unless separately scoped.
Success criteria could duplicate test-builder responsibilities; the gate should define what success means before tests, not replace the test strategy.
